paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: : The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioGPT and Llama2, where “Base” denotes LLM without editing.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of knowledge probing after applying various editing methods to LLMs, with “Base” representing the model without any editing. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10³, with tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 60 to 80 percent. Five distinct lines represent the editing methods: “Base” (black line with circle markers), “MEND” (brown line with diamond markers), “FT” (blue line with triangle markers), “MEMIT” (purple line with star markers), and “ROME” (green line with square markers). The “Base” line starts at approximately 63% and increases to about 68% over the range. The “MEND” line begins at around 69% and rises to approximately 77%. The “FT” line starts at roughly 64% and increases to about 70%. The “MEMIT” line begins at approximately 68% and rises to about 75%. The “ROME” line starts at around 73% and increases to approximately 81%. All lines show a general upward trend as the co-occurrence number increases, with “ROME” consistently achieving the highest accuracy and “Base” the lowest.
